title: Hi - I'm building a tool to generate game assets, can you rate this one?
author: riccioverde11
selftext: What do you think? Does it feel AI-slop? This is a spine-asset.

comments.author: gholias
comments.body:
Im also working on something like that using Spine. Any simple animation like that one you posted are okayish, but anything more complex fails miserably.

Try a humanoid walk cycle. Unfortunately AI can’t no generate them yet.

replies.author: riccioverde11
replies.body: Let me try it, I already experimented and was working miracles tbh.

replies.author: gholias
replies.body: This looks better than what I was able to achieve. Last night I pivot to use sedance to generate videos to feed the ai model to cut into frames

replies.author: Post-reality
replies.body: My game has thousands of on top of hundreds of layers with extremely complicated animation with consistent style- it's possible, but people on this sub seem to be unfamiliar with frontier design tools which enterprise companies already incorporated into their workflows. I assume it has to do with costs and lack of expertise (or the experts just lurk). But yeah, you may still need to do some post-production polish, especially when it comes to animations.

replies.author: riccioverde11
replies.body: The tool actually is made on purpose to keep visual consistency across animations, i didn't want to share a lot of the tool, simply cause i'd like to first understand if the assets generated felt "ai-ish".

replies.author: Post-reality
replies.body: There are already such tools. The question is whether or not you can compete against them, even if as a niche (developers sometimes use multiple tools in case their favourite fails to do what they want/need)

replies.author: riccioverde11
replies.body: Can you share one which works?

replies.author: Post-reality
replies.body: There are many of them, such Auto-Sprite V2, Ludo, Scenario and SpriteFlow. Also, PixelLab, but I dislike the pixel art style, and prefer the more modern "flashy" artatyles of the early 2000's. Anyway, not trying to discourge you, because there's plenty of room for multiple service providers so good luck with it!

replies.author: riccioverde11
replies.body: They all suck tbh, tried all of them

replies.author: gholias
replies.body: I actually just tried autosprite-v3 and it is working very well. Still have to do some cleanup, but Im liking the results
